decisions.question: How many tasks, and where do the four canonical orders go in the task sequence?

options.label: 6 tasks: FunctionRef, inputs and edges, canonical orders, definition, findings, verification
options.consequence: Each library change is one reviewable unit; the claim-order design (a routed item) gets its own review; the definition task stays focused on well-formedness.

options.label: 5 tasks: the canonical orders folded into the definition task
options.consequence: One task fewer; the definition task carries a second design decision (the claim order) that nothing in it uses.

options.label: 4 tasks: edges and definition together
options.consequence: Fewer reviews, but one task would turn six cases green and mix two rule sets.

decisions.chosen: 6 tasks: FunctionRef, inputs and edges, canonical orders, definition, findings, verification
decisions.why: writing-plans splits where a reviewer could reject one task and approve its neighbour; the comparators (the routed claim-order question) and the definition's rules are separable, and 6 is within the cap of 7. The dry run ran exactly this sequence and each task's failing and passing steps behaved as the plan states.

decisions.question: D4 puts the canonical orders in lib/src/ir/, but the claim order compares ShellClaim, which lib/src/graph/graph.dart declares and which imports lib/src/ir/ (routed from S116). Where does the claim order live?

options.label: in lib/src/ir/ over the claim's parts (a ClaimKey record of source, scope, writes)
options.consequence: All four orders sit together where D4 puts them; ir/ never imports graph/; nidana.model.11 passes each claim's three fields.

options.label: in lib/src/graph/ beside ShellClaim
options.consequence: No record type, but the four orders are split across two libraries against D4's wording, and this phase could not test the claim order before nidana.model.11.

options.label: in lib/src/ir/ naming ShellClaim
options.consequence: Makes ir/ and graph/ import each other (legal in Dart, but the routed item asks to avoid it).

decisions.chosen: in lib/src/ir/ over the claim's parts (a ClaimKey record of source, scope, writes)
decisions.why: Keeps D4's placement and the import direction graph/ -> ir/, and lets this phase pin the claim order with tests now. A test reads lib/src/ir/ for import or export directives naming graph/ so the boundary stays pinned.

decisions.question: Does compareClaimKeys trust that each claim's writes iterate in canonical order (ShellClaim keeps them so), or sort copies itself?

options.label: sort copies of both writes
options.consequence: Correct for any Iterable a caller passes; costs a sort per comparison over small sets.

options.label: compare in iteration order
options.consequence: Cheaper, but a comparator over parts would depend on a caller's precondition; dry run D10 shows the difference.

decisions.why: The comparator takes parts, not a ShellClaim, so it should not rely on the caller having sorted them; claims hold few topics, and the Interface's 'element by element in canonical order' then holds whatever the iterable. Pinned by a test that compares {x, y} with [y, x].

decisions.question: The topology order is 'by topologyId'. Is the shared comparator over TopologyDefinition or over ids?

options.label: over ids: compareTopologyIds(String, String)
options.consequence: canonical_order.dart does not import definition.dart (which imports it), and TopologyCycle.topologyIds sorts by the same comparator.

options.label: over definitions: compareTopologies(TopologyDefinition, TopologyDefinition)
options.consequence: Reads better at the graph's call site, but makes definition.dart and canonical_order.dart import each other.

decisions.why: Same reasoning as the claim order: comparators over parts keep the imports one-way, and one comparator then serves both the graph's topologies (nidana.model.11) and a cycle's ids.

decisions.question: Where do the comparators and the sorted-copy helper live, and are they public within the package?

options.label: new internal library lib/src/ir/canonical_order.dart, top-level functions, exported by no public library
options.consequence: One file per responsibility; package tests import it from src as lineage_test.dart already does; exports_test.dart is unchanged.

options.label: private functions inside definition.dart
options.consequence: No new file, but findings.dart and graph.dart could not reach them.

decisions.chosen: new internal library lib/src/ir/canonical_order.dart, top-level functions, exported by no public library
decisions.why: D4 names lib/src/ir/ for the canonical orders and three libraries use them; top-level public names in a src library are not public API (no public library exports them), and the analyzer's unused_element does not apply to them, so compareClaimKeys can land before its first caller in nidana.model.11.

decisions.question: Do the package tests pin which argument an ArgumentError names, beyond the suite's throwsArgumentError?

options.label: pin ArgumentError.name for every rejection
options.consequence: Each rejection is attributed to its argument (inputs, transformer, duration, retry, combinator, topic, topologyId, transforms, name); a check made in the wrong place fails a test.

options.label: only throwsArgumentError, as the suite does
options.consequence: Shorter tests; a factory that rejects for the wrong reason passes.

decisions.why: The contract says only ArgumentError; naming the argument costs nothing and is what a person debugging a misbuilt edge needs. It also fixes the check order for single-fault inputs. Messages stay free, except the S132 rule against 'an {variant}'.

decisions.question: How is the stage-edge table encoded in TransformEdge.stage?

options.label: a private record per combinator (_StageRule) from one exhaustive switch, then generic checks
options.consequence: The table reads like the contract's table and the switch fails to compile when a CombinatorKind is added.

options.label: per-combinator if-chains in the factory
options.consequence: No extra types, but the table is spread over branches and harder to review against the contract.

decisions.chosen: a private record per combinator (_StageRule) from one exhaustive switch, then generic checks
decisions.why: Declarative over imperative (owner's preference); the switch is exhaustive over CombinatorKind, and reduceInto's arm throws, which is how stage rejects it. Checks run combinator, inputs, transformer, duration presence, duration sign, retry.
evidence: hsdd/contract/topology-ir.md What a stage edge holds

decisions.question: FunctionRef.of when the rendering has the marker but no closing quote; and how is the name read?

options.label: anonymous; String.indexOf, no RegExp
options.consequence: Matches 'anonymous when that text is absent or empty'; unreachable on the VM; no allocation of a pattern.

options.label: the rest of the rendering as the name
options.consequence: A name the rule does not define.

decisions.why: G9's rule defines the name as the text between the marker and the next quote; with no next quote there is no such text. F1 R re-checked every form the tests use on the pinned SDK.

decisions.question: How does FunctionRef.named check its name, given the class keeps a final field?

options.label: initializer list : name = _nonEmpty(name), a library function that throws
options.consequence: No constructor body; the parameter keeps its name; non-const as the Interface declares.

options.label: an initializing formal with a constructor body that throws
options.consequence: Works, but the body reads the parameter through the field's nullable type.

decisions.chosen: initializer list : name = _nonEmpty(name), a library function that throws
decisions.why: Smallest change that fulfils the routed item; the same initializer-list style the findings' sorting constructors use.

decisions.question: G6 rejects a negative StageInput, but StageInput asserts a non-negative index and dart test runs with assertions, so no test can build one in-process. Pin it, and how?

options.label: a package test that runs a small program through Platform.resolvedExecutable without assertions
options.consequence: Pins the rule (dry run D4 is otherwise invisible to every test and to the gate); one subprocess, the whole package run stays about 4 seconds.

options.label: pin it in the experiment only
options.consequence: No process in the package tests; the rule then has no test in the gate.

options.label: leave it to review
options.consequence: Cheapest; the check could be dropped silently.

decisions.chosen: a package test that runs a small program through Platform.resolvedExecutable without assertions
decisions.why: The run ruling asks for tests where a rule would otherwise go unpinned; the dry run showed the test passes with the check and fails without it, starts no flutter, and leaves no file behind (temp directory torn down).

decisions.question: How does a test reproduce S132's routed corner, two state topics whose value types render alike?

options.label: a helper library test/src/cart_elsewhere.dart declaring a second Cart, imported with a prefix
options.consequence: The test builds two real StateTopics that are unequal Topics with equal refs, exactly the corner nidana.model.11 will meet.

options.label: two TopicRefs built apart with typeName 'Cart'
options.consequence: No extra file, but it only restates the second-state-sink rule and never shows two distinct types.

decisions.chosen: a helper library test/src/cart_elsewhere.dart declaring a second Cart, imported with a prefix
decisions.why: The corner is about types that differ but render alike; only two class declarations in two libraries produce it. One five-line file.

decisions.question: Do the findings' constructors also make their lists unmodifiable copies now, or only sort them?

options.label: sort into unmodifiable copies
options.consequence: G3's value side lands with the value semantics; the G3 case that also covers findings passes on this part once nidana.model.11 lands graphs.

options.label: sort into growable lists, leave G3 to a later phase
options.consequence: A later phase would have to touch the same constructors again.

decisions.why: The Scope says 'value semantics' of the findings and G3 names findings; sorting already copies, so unmodifiable costs nothing.

decisions.question: Do the IR values and findings gain toString overrides, which would make test failures readable?

options.label: no toString
options.consequence: Matches the Interface, which declares none, and nidana.model.9's ruling for TopologyRef; failures print 'Instance of ...'.

options.label: add toString
options.consequence: Readable failures, but a behavior the contract does not state.

decisions.why: Precedent (nidana.model.9 plan, Interface rule) and the run's governance freeze: a rendering is a contract decision; already routed to the end-of-node sweep for topic-model values.

decisions.question: How much code does the plan carry for spot-check-tier Sonnet implementers?

options.label: full test files, the stage-edge table, canonical_order.dart and the findings' constructors verbatim; other bodies as signatures and rules
options.consequence: Implementers write exactly the tested code; the plan is 1770 lines, about the length of nidana.model.9's 1737.

options.label: test names and key assertions only
options.consequence: Half the length, but each implementer reconstructs 1054 lines of tests and the expected counts no longer hold.

decisions.chosen: full test files, the stage-edge table, canonical_order.dart and the findings' constructors verbatim; other bodies as signatures and rules
decisions.why: Precedent and the dry run: every quoted block is the formatter-stable draft the dry run ran (X), so each task's expected output in the plan is measured, not guessed.

decisions.question: Is the conformance suite's failure to reach three rules (retry on combinators other than map, G6's negative index, edge order in a definition's equality) a contract gap to report, or only a learning?

options.label: both: a low-severity contract gap and a Learning routed to the end-of-node sweep
options.consequence: hsdd-contract can add two assertions and one not-executable line within v1; the phase is not blocked.

options.label: a Learning only
options.consequence: The governance owner might not see the missing not-executable line ADR-001 item 3 asks for.

decisions.chosen: both: a low-severity contract gap and a Learning routed to the end-of-node sweep
decisions.why: Same treatment S127 gave the recording suite's misses. suite_reach.txt shows seeded defects D5 and D11 pass every G5 to G7 case even once G3 and G7 join the restriction; D4 is unreachable under assertions.

decisions.question: Which five input classes go in Review Focus?

options.label: hash-collection keys, reused argument lists, repeated topics and variants under one name, rendered-alike types, transformer forms the suite does not name
options.consequence: Each is a way a consumer (graphs, catalog, projection) will use the IR, and three pass the gate's replay when broken (dry run D2, D8; D3 is caught).

options.label: include the negative index and per-combinator retry
options.consequence: Both are rules, not input classes a user meets, and both are already pinned.

decisions.chosen: hash-collection keys, reused argument lists, repeated topics and variants under one name, rendered-alike types, transformer forms the suite does not name
decisions.why: writing-plans asks for the inputs most likely to bite a person using the software; nidana.model.11 to .14 build graphs, sets and catalogs over these values next.

experiments.question: Does this plan's task sequence, run in a temporary copy of HEAD 06d90bc with the drafted files, produce the failing and passing outputs the plan states, keep every committed fixture and test green, and catch seeded defects? Also: how Object.hash treats lists, whether hash codes are stable across runs, what Set.unmodifiable keeps, and what FunctionRef.of's rule yields for the forms the tests use.
experiments.finding: Yes. Package tests 147 -> 153 -> 160 -> 166 -> 174 -> 182; the gate's restricted topology-ir replay goes 1/10 (S1) -> 10/10 after Task 4; the full gate exits 0 (G); unrestricted 11/43 (U, G7's IR case passes early); fixture diagnostics unchanged at 3143 in 70 libraries (B, A); every quoted block formatter-stable (X). Object.hash of a list hashes identity (H2), Object.hashAll is element-wise and order-sensitive (H3, H4); Object.hash and enum hash codes change between runs (F2), so no test pins a value. Set.unmodifiable keeps first-occurrence order, copies, throws UnsupportedError (U1 to U4); Set == is identity (U6). FunctionRef.of: topLevel, reduce, label, identity, Box., Box.named, call, _private@21481238; anonymous for extension tear-offs and every closure (R). 13 seeded defects: all fail a package test, 10 pass the gate's replay (D).

experiments.question: Would topology-ir@v1's suite catch the seeded defects once G3, G5, G6 and G7 are all in the restriction (nidana.model.11's gate)?
experiments.finding: D2 and D7 fail G7's IR case; D5 (retry accepted on combine) and D11 (definition equality ignores edge order) pass every G5 to G7 case; D8 is not distinguishable here because both G3 cases fail on graphs until nidana.model.11. Output in suite_reach.txt.

contract_gaps.where: hsdd/contract/topology-ir.md G6 and ## Validation; hsdd/contract/fixture/topology-ir/behavior/topology_ir_conformance.dart 'G6 a definition rejects an empty id and ill-formed edges' (line 714)
contract_gaps.problem: Low, non-blocking. G6 rejects 'a stage input that is negative', but no fixture covers that part: StageInput asserts a non-negative index and every binding runs under dart test with assertions enabled, so the assertion fires before any TopologyDefinition sees the index. ADR-001 item 3 asks a guarantee covered only in part to carry a not-executable line for the rest; topology-ir@v1's Validation has none for G6. nidana.model.10's package tests pin it by running a program without assertions.
contract_gaps.proposed_fix: Compatible hsdd-contract touch within v1: add '- not executable: G6's negative stage input, StageInput asserts a non-negative index and every binding runs with assertions enabled; checked by nidana.model's gates' to topology-ir@v1's Validation.

contract_gaps.where: hsdd/contract/fixture/topology-ir/behavior/topology_ir_conformance.dart, the G5 case at line 607 and the G7 case at line 774
contract_gaps.problem: Low, non-blocking. The suite checks a retry's rejection on map only, so a TransformEdge.stage that accepts a retry on combine (or any combinator but switchMap) passes every G5 case; and no G7 assertion compares two definitions that differ only in edge order, so a definition equality that ignores edge order passes. Seeded defects D5 and D11 pass every G5, G6 and G7 case (docs/auto-run/experiments/ir-values-plan/suite_reach.txt). nidana.model.10's package tests pin both.
contract_gaps.proposed_fix: Compatible hsdd-contract touch within v1, at the end-of-node governance sweep: in the G5 case, loop the retry rejection over every combinator but switchMap; in the G7 IR case, assert that a definition with two sink edges swapped is not equal to the original.
